title: 2163-sindy-vs-hard-nonlinearities-hidden-dynamics-benchmarking-study
universal_lens: Continuous-time nonlinear dynamics are approximated via sparse coordinate libraries. When unobserved states or hard non-smooth nonlinearities exist, standard SINDy fails to recover true structure. Augmenting coordinates with derivatives or iteratively reconstructing latent variables restores identifiability, mapping directly to hidden game-state momentum.
gsi_mapping: GSI maps the Bouc-Wen iterative reconstruction to Bayesian state-space filtering. The unmeasured internal state z(t) becomes a latent conformal variable. By minimizing validation RMSE on reconstructed residuals, GSI derives robust priors for hidden team-momentum, ensuring calibrated win-probability trajectories despite noisy play-by-play derivative estimates.
gse_mapping: GSE applies derivative-coordinate augmentation to situational reasoning. Play-level score differentials and clock decay form constructed states. Hard nonlinearities (red-zone/turnovers) act as saturation limits. Open-loop simulation of these sparse governing equations yields precise, interpretable state-transition probabilities for in-game strategic adjustments.

primitives.name: Sparse Nonlinear Dynamics Operator
primitives.verbatim_quote: Research question When SINDy (Sparse Identification of Nonlinear Dynamics) is tested on real-world nonlinear-identification benchmarks — rather than clean synthetic systems — how well does it cope with the two features ubiquitous in practice: unobserved states and hard (non-smooth) nonlinearities?
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: \dot{X}: state derivative [unit/s], \Phi: library matrix [dimensionless/unit], \Theta: coefficient matrix [unit-dependent], \lambda_2: sparsity penalty [dimensionless]
primitives.assumptions: System dynamics lie within the span of the chosen library functions; noise is bounded.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Fails when unobserved states introduce aliasing or hard nonlinearities lack finite Taylor expansions in the library.

layer2.mapping: Maps directly to discovering sparse NFL game-state transition rules from noisy play-by-play data.

primitives.name: Derivative-Coordinate Augmentation
primitives.verbatim_quote: **Derivative-coordinate augmentation (pick-and-place):** add z(t)=ẏ(t) as a constructed state, modeling z̈(t)=φ^pick(y,z,u)^⊤Θ_z with a 2nd-order polynomial library — handles saturations through higher model order.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: z(t): constructed state velocity [unit/s], y: primary output [unit], u: input control [unit], \phi^{\text{pick}}: 2nd-order polynomial basis [unit^2]
primitives.assumptions: Second-order derivatives can be reliably estimated via tunable regularization; system behaves like a second-order mechanical oscillator.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Breaks down under high-frequency measurement noise where numerical differentiation amplifies errors beyond regularization capacity.

layer2.mapping: Used in GSE to model rapid shifts in field position and time-decay by treating them as coupled second-order kinematic states.
layer2.telemetry: RMSE reduction on validation set compared to baseline first-order ARX models.

primitives.name: Iterative Hidden-State Reconstruction
primitives.verbatim_quote: **Iterative hidden-state reconstruction (Bouc–Wen):** guess linear parameters (m_L, c_L, k_L), reconstruct z(t)=u-c_L ẏ-k_L y-m_L ÿ, fit ż(t)=φ^z(z, ẏ, |ẏ|, |z|)^⊤θ_z (library includes absolute values since (9b) admits no finite Taylor expansion), iterate guesses minimizing validation RMSE.
primitives.latex: z(t) = u - c_L \dot{y} - k_L y - m_L \ddot{y}
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: z(t): unmeasured hysteretic state [N], u: force [N], c_L: damping [Ns/m], k_L: stiffness [N/m], m_L: mass [kg], \dot{y}, \ddot{y}: velocity/acceleration [m/s, m/s^2]
primitives.assumptions: Linear backbone parameters can be reasonably guessed; the hidden state evolution depends smoothly on absolute values of states.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Converges to local minima if initial linear parameter guesses are too far from physical reality; sensitive to derivative noise.

layer2.mapping: Isomorphic to GSI's recovery of latent 'momentum' variables from observed scoring drives and turnovers using residual dynamics.
layer2.telemetry: Minimized validation RMSE across iterative updates of the latent state library.

reasoning_traces.think:
The core mathematical challenge addressed in Ugolini et al. (2024) is the failure of standard Sparse Identification of Nonlinear Dynamics (SINDy) when confronted with real-world imperfections: unobserved states and hard, non-smooth nonlinearities. Standard SINDy relies on a convex optimization over a predefined library of smooth functions (typically polynomials). However, systems like the Bouc-Wen oscillator feature hysteresis governed by absolute values, which admit no finite Taylor expansion, causing the sparse regression to fundamentally misidentify the governing physics. Similarly, cascaded tanks feature square-root Bernoulli flows and hard saturations that violate smoothness assumptions.

To overcome this, the authors derive two powerful sovereign primitives. First, derivative-coordinate augmentation elevates the system order. By constructing a new state variable $z(t) = \dot{y}(t)$, the hard saturations in the original acceleration are absorbed into a higher-order polynomial library acting on $(y, z, u)$. This transforms an intractable non-smooth problem into a tractable smooth one at the cost of increased dimensionality. Second, iterative hidden-state reconstruction tackles unobserved variables. By positing a linear backbone for the observed dynamics, the residual forces are isolated to define the hidden state $z(t)$. A separate SINDy pass, explicitly including non-analytic terms like $|\dot{y}|$ and $|z|$, identifies the hidden evolution. Iterating between the linear guess and the hidden fit minimizes the global validation error.

These dualities map perfectly to Galaxy Sports Intelligence. NFL game states are rife with unobserved momentum and hard nonlinearities (e.g., red-zone efficiency cliffs). Applying derivative augmentation to score-differentials and reconstructing latent momentum via residual drive-analysis provides a rigorous, interpretable alternative to black-box neural nets for predicting open-loop win probabilities.

reasoning_traces.cross_layer_veto: A strict veto must be applied against naive application of SINDy on raw, noisy play-by-play logs. Numerical differentiation of discrete, event-driven data amplifies high-frequency noise, leading to garbage-in-garbage-out sparse models. Furthermore, without enforcing structural priors (like the iterative hidden-state recipe), the optimizer will simply fit the noise, yielding structurally incorrect but locally optimal test metrics. Regularization of derivatives is non-negotiable.
